findings.reason: two implementations with different user-visible surfaces both satisfy the stated measure, so the section must name the replacement summary text and assert it.
findings.text: §2 omits the count sentence for the shell path but never says what the `plan-summary` meta then carries, and its done-when only requires the three count phrases to be absent from that meta, so a node may drop it entirely and still pass while `docs/ui/plan.jsx:1274` renders `PG.summary` — every append-created record would then show a blank summary

findings.reason: an unstated refusal surface is a behaviour change the node meets mid-build with no instruction on whether to keep, carve out or test it.
findings.text: §3 states the store refusal "runs today only for `insert_section` and `append_evidence`", but a third site already refuses the term: a `sections.<id>.body` set reaches `_refuse_forged_body_structure` through `_require_authored_value` (`reckon/_store_section_ops.py:141`, `reckon/_store.py:1074`), so widening `_DEFERRED_WORK_TERM` also widens a refusal §3 does not account for, and a legacy section body carrying "goes to §4" can no longer be re-set except in text mode

findings.reason: the commit is named and the quoted state resolves there, so the root-cause argument stands unchanged for a reader who checks it.
findings.text: §1 says the record "says '0 committed run(s)…'" in the present tense, but that path now reads "14 committed run(s), 64 section-anchored comment(s), and 47 landed commit(s)" after the rebuild at `c058d9c74`, and the zero sentence exists only at the cited close commit `f7f7d2d6d`

response_events.note: §2 now names the shell's summary, 'Landing record for <plan title>: evidence appended by section', and asserts it in the plan-summary meta.

done_when-1.note: §2 now names the shell's summary, 'Landing record for <plan title>: evidence appended by section', and asserts it in the plan-summary meta.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §1's zero-count quotation resolves at the cited close commit but not in the file on disk today; every other named symbol, line anchor and plan reference resolves.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §2's measure cannot tell a record with no `plan-summary` meta from one carrying a count-free summary, and the SPA renders that meta.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every gate log is required under the run directory, which is durable and outside any node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test filenames, `data-evidence-origin`, `lost_anchors` and `_DEFERRED_WORK_TERM` name mechanisms, and no plan label, stage name or ticket number reaches them.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §3 under-states where the deferred-work refusal already runs; the root cause in §1 matches its cited evidence and each section's mechanism does produce its own done-when, with `_landed_record_shell` and `_apply_evidence_appends` named as the callers.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each section names one deliverable; §4's mark, carry-forward, refusal and loss list are one mechanism measured by one done-when block.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-after: a-finished-plan-closes` resolves to `docs/plans/a-finished-plan-closes.html`, the project's unwired-plan check reports nothing against the plan, and `plan-section-depends-on` wires s3→s2 and s4→{s2,s3}, which matches the `reckon/_store.py` write sharing the sections declare.
